mbm-1651.clue: The onions get top billing in my sketchbook.
mbm-1651.quote: I painted the kitchen before anyone woke up. The sun lit three onions in a blue bowl like actors under a spotlight. Mum saw the canvas and moved breakfast to the other table.

mbm-1652.clue: One cupcake survives every family party.
mbm-1652.quote: I crocheted a pink cupcake to mark the chair of honor. My youngest cousin tried to peel off the yarn wrapper. Now he checks all the cakes very carefully before picking one.

mbm-1653.clue: I got the whole courtyard to sing one name.
mbm-1653.quote: The first verse of our son goes out to a neighbor. We kept singing the name of an absent friend until he came round the corner still carrying his groceries. He took the lead with a pineapple in each arm.

mbm-1654.clue: I've been putting the island back together.
mbm-1654.quote: Our kayak club found the little island almost hidden behind floating bottles. We paddled out with onion sacks. By lunch we had eight bags, a clean pebble beach and one delighted sandpiper standing in charge.

mbm-1655.clue: My game's first customer is a goose.
mbm-1655.quote: I wrote a little shopkeeping game and forgot to give the first customer any money. Now the pixel goose pays for everything with feathers. Everyone asks for more geese.

mbm-1656.clue: I keep an orange pencil in my jump log.
mbm-1656.quote: The drop-zone café uses orange pencils for breakfast orders. I borrowed one to fill out my first jump log and returned it after my hundredth. The cook looked at the stub and declared it much too short to order eggs.

mbm-1657.clue: I left one fish swimming the wrong way.
mbm-1657.quote: My sister asked for a school of fish on her quilt. I turned one toward the edge because there's always somebody who sees the ice-cream van first. She knew which fish was me.

mbm-1658.clue: The newspaper remembers my last trick.
mbm-1658.quote: I tore yesterday's paper and opened a whole sheet with a flourish. Grandpa checked the date, folded it up, and asked if I could please do tomorrow's crossword next.

mbm-1659.clue: My jacket's loudest part is under the collar.
mbm-1659.quote: I lined my black jacket with a scrap of my dad's old trumpet-print tie. Push my collar up a little and one brass bell peeks out, ready for a solo.

mbm-1660.clue: I've got one scarf that only appears at breakfast.
mbm-1660.quote: I practiced pulling silk from my fist over the toaster, where the morning light is good. My niece started tying a tiny scarf to the marmalade spoon. I let her have the last trick.

mbm-1661.clue: I carry my spare key in a very little boat.
mbm-1661.quote: I carved a cork key float shaped like my kayak. When I dropped the key at the dock, we fished the little kayak out with the big one. My friend took a photo of the rescue.

mbm-1662.clue: I've never missed a movie for the bus.
mbm-1662.quote: My best friend and I split the rows on our last trip to the cinema. From my seat I saw her glasses catch the brightest scene. When we missed the bus, we drew it for each other on the ticket backs.

mbm-1663.clue: I carry two pencils and use them both sideways.
mbm-1663.quote: My niece likes the chipping green but hates scorecards. After each shot we rub the raised number on the flag stand onto our paper. She's filled a page with sevens.

mbm-1664.clue: I've got a nest that hangs from the kettle.
mbm-1664.quote: I crocheted a round potholder from scraps of brown yarn. The loop curled in on itself like a nest. Mum puts her teaspoons in it and calls them the silver chicks.

mbm-1665.clue: I never throw away the blue half of the ticket.
mbm-1665.quote: Our cinema used two-color tickets for double features. I pasted the blue halves around a mirror. Most mornings I recognize the movie from the color of my shirt in the middle.

mbm-1666.clue: The kitchen door takes the first turn.
mbm-1666.quote: We rehearsed a tango in the café before the chairs went out. When my partner opened the swing door for the flour delivery, I spun through on the beat. The baker asked for an encore.

mbm-1667.clue: I can get a whole chord out of three cousins.
mbm-1667.quote: At family gatherings we each sing the note on the colored peg we're holding. When Grandpa wants the last chord to hang there, he clips all three pegs to his jacket.

mbm-1668.clue: I practice above the washing basket.
mbm-1668.quote: The first time I kept three beanbags up for a minute, the buzzer on the dryer went. I dropped all three straight into the clean towels. That's a good landing by my standards.

mbm-1669.clue: My goggles have a tiny blue star in the case.
mbm-1669.quote: A kid on the next swim team traded me a little sticker for a spare cap at a meet. We look for the blue star in the bleachers now, long before we look at the lane list.

mbm-1670.clue: I have a good reason for saving the lemonade cap.
mbm-1670.quote: At the drive-in our little radio knob fell off during the quiet scene. I slid a bottle cap over the spindle and turned the sound back up. It still fits snugly in the glove box.

mbm-1671.clue: Nobody else takes a ruler to the cinema.
mbm-1671.quote: I caught my height against an old film poster every birthday. The owner remembered me when I went back and showed me the pencil marks behind a newer frame. I'd made it above the hero's hat.

mbm-1672.clue: I made a sweater for the jam first.
mbm-1672.quote: I wanted to crochet a cardigan and started with a little jar cozy to learn the pattern. The jam jar fit perfectly on the first try. Everyone had a lovely breakfast while I undid sleeve number two.

mbm-1673.clue: I bring a pencil to the moving rock.
mbm-1673.quote: On our hillside trail a boulder looks balanced on one corner. I draw it from the same spot every year. It hasn't moved a hair, but my first drawing has my little sister barely tall enough to see over it.

mbm-1674.clue: I like a dance floor with one squeaky board.
mbm-1674.quote: Our old hall has a floorboard that sings when my partner hits the turn. At the competition we danced on perfect polished wood. Halfway through I whispered squeak and she grinned.

mbm-1675.clue: I cut the smallest sun for the biggest window.
mbm-1675.quote: When I unfolded my first sheet of papel picado the little sun was lopsided. We hung it over the wide kitchen window. At breakfast its shadow sits neatly in the middle of my plate.
